data.body:
Fix pushed as Gerrit change 1050 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1050), on its own branch off origin/main rather than inside the provider-seam stack — the defect is unrelated to that epic and should land independently so the stack can rebase onto it.

SCOPE: 39 files, 41 insertions / 41 deletions. sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod) -> sys.modules[name] = mod. No production code, no test logic changed. tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_stale_binding_404.py was already correct (it registers under a file-unique key and says so); its docstring is the only remaining mention of the old pattern, left deliberately as documentation of the trap.

LOCAL VERIFICATION: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -> 1576 passed; the diffing/ cluster that fails in CI -> 237 passed; ruff check + format clean.

HONEST LIMIT ON THAT VERIFICATION, which matters given this ticket is about order-dependent failures: I could NOT reproduce the original failure locally. My venv is py3.14; the failing CI job is macos-latest/py3.13. So local green is consistent with the fix but does not DEMONSTRATE it — CI on change 1050, and then the rebased provider-seam stack, are the real reproducers. This is the same evidence-provenance problem epic 3147 exists to address: the instrument I verified with could not exhibit the failure.

WHY THE FIX IS STILL SOUND INDEPENDENT OF REPRODUCTION: the defect is not probabilistic, it is a straightforward object-identity bug readable from the source. setdefault keeps a previously-registered module while the caller execs into and returns a different one, so two class objects with the same qualified name coexist and isinstance between them is False by definition. Assignment makes registered-module and returned-module the same object by construction, which is the invariant every caller already assumed.
